Our Vision & Values
'To deliver a curriculum that is provided by good teachers underpinned by an effective blueprint for excellence in culture, behaviour, attainment and wellbeing - to find the champion in everyone.'
Our school values are an important part of our school identity and were created following suggestions and recommendations from members of our first-generation community. Our values underpin all we do every day to ensure that children in our care as well as all stakeholders are supported to be the best that they can be.

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome from the Headteacher - Lime Wood Primary School
pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Headteacher
Since opening our doors in September 2023 to our very first Reception class, Lime Wood Primary School has grown alongside our wonderful community. As our school has developed, so too have the opportunities we provide for our children, including the opening of our Specialist Resource Provision in Autumn 2025, enabling us to support an even wider range of learners.
We are proud to be at the heart of the Erith Hills Quarry community and believe that strong partnerships with parents, carers, residents and local organisations are key to helping every child flourish. By working together and listening to our community, we strive to provide an education that inspires children to become confident, compassionate and lifelong learners.
As Headteacher, I feel both honoured and privileged to lead this nurturing and ambitious school. Early in my career, I was inspired by American educator Rita Pierson's belief that "Every child needs a champion." That message has shaped my approach to education ever since and reflects the Woodland Academy Trust's ethos of "Ignite the spark, reveal the champion."
This philosophy underpins everything we do and is reflected in our school vision:
Since opening, our dedicated staff, governors and wider community have worked together to create a school where every child is known, valued and encouraged to thrive. I am incredibly proud that, in our first Ofsted inspection since opening, inspectors recognised Lime Wood as "a highly inclusive school" where leaders, governors and staff "work with determination to ensure that every pupil succeeds." They also praised our nurturing relationships, ambitious curriculum and positive culture, recognising the values that underpin everything we do.
As we continue to grow, we remain excited about the future and the opportunities ahead. Each year we welcome new children, families and colleagues who all play an important part in shaping our school community. Together, we will continue to build a school where every child can flourish and every success is celebrated.
I hope our website gives you a glimpse into life at Lime Wood Primary School. You can find out more about what makes our school unique by visiting our Why Choose Lime Wood Primary School page.
If you would like to arrange a visit or discuss joining our growing school community, please do get in touch. We would be delighted to welcome you.
2 Sandy Road, Erith, Kent DA8 1FJ

pageCache.pageTitle: Inclusion Base (Specialist Resource Provision) - Lime Wood Primary School
pageCache.text:
Inclusion Base (Specialist Resource Provision)
Tiny Seed opened in November 2025 and provided places for 12–15 children with an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) where the primary need is Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) and/or speech, language and communication needs (SLCN).
In September 2026, we extended the provisions:
EYFS - Tiny Seed - 8 places
KS1 - Giving Tree - 10 places
KS2 (Y3) - Lemonade Tree - 10 places
Our Inclusion Bases are designed to offer specialist support within a mainstream school environment, helping children achieve academically, socially, and emotionally.
Our Inclusion Base reflects this vision by providing a nurturing and inclusive environment where children with ASD and SLCN can grow in confidence and thrive.
Recognised by OfstedIn our first Ofsted inspection since opening, inspectors recognised the positive impact of our Inclusion Base (Specialist Resource Provision) and the school's commitment to providing high-quality, inclusive support for children with additional needs.
What Ofsted said about Tiny Seed⭐ "The specialist resourced provision for pupils with SEND has been thoughtfully developed."
⭐ "The teaching and care it provides have a consistently positive impact on pupils' wellbeing and progress."
⭐ "Staff receive regular training so that they can meet pupils' complex needs confidently."
The team is made up of dedicated professionals who are passionate about creating a nurturing and inclusive environment for every child. Our highly committed team brings a wealth of experience in supporting children with ASD and SLCN.
Visit our 'Staff Team' page to meet our SRP team!
Admissions to our Inclusion Base (SRP) are managed through the Bexley SEND EHCP panel (not through the school’s main admissions process).
EligibilityChildren may be considered if they:
ApplicationsIf you believe our provision may be suitable for your child, please contact your case officer at Bexley Local Authority.
Inclusion Base Information Booklet
For full details about the support, admissions process, and services linked to our inclusion bases, please read our Information Booklet below.
➡️Read the Inclusion Bases Information Booklet
The Inclusion Base (SRP) forms part of the Bexley Local Offer, designed to give children and young people with SEND access to high-quality local education and support. By expanding local specialist capacity, the provision helps reduce the need for out-of-borough placements and keeps children learning closer to home.
At Lime Wood, we are committed to working in partnership with families, ensuring parents and carers are actively involved in their child’s journey.
For general enquiries about our Inclusion Bases (SRP), please contact:Lime Wood Primary School by calling 01322 344939 or emailing us at [email protected]. You can also use our website Contact Form
For admissions queries please contact your case officer.
2 Sandy Road, Erith, Kent DA8 1FJ

pageCache.pageTitle: Children's University  - Lime Wood Primary School
pageCache.text:
Children's University
All of the schools in the Woodland Academy Trust are part of London South East Children’s University, an award programme that encourages children to get involved in lots of exciting activities and experiences in their local area. All school sites are recognised Learning Destinations, and all of our extra-curricular clubs are validated through Children’s University.
From EYFS, children receive their own Passport to Learning and gain a stamp for every hour of activity completed at a validated Learning Destination, as they work towards their Children’s University Award, Certificate, Diploma, Degree and eventually Fellowship. At the end of each year, children who have earned enough stamps are invited to a special university-style graduation ceremony to celebrate their success!
There are lots of Learning Destinations that have already signed up to the London South East Children’s University, from kayaking on Danson Lake to following in the footsteps of Charles Darwin at Downe House, with plenty more places and activities looking to get involved.
For more information take a look at our Partnerships page too.
2 Sandy Road, Erith, Kent DA8 1FJ
Email: [email protected]

pageCache.pageTitle: Modern Foreign Languages  - Lime Wood Primary School
pageCache.text:
Modern Foreign Languages
We teach Spanish to all of our children in Key Stage Two (from year 3 and above). A majority of the learning takes place through Language Angels which the children find interactive and engaging.
Our intent is to provide broad linguistic and cultural experiences for our pupils that enable them to foster a love of languages and to develop their communication skills. We endeavour to broaden the cultural awareness of our pupils, to create linguists who enjoy learning languages and who can express themselves confidently in the second most spoken language in the world.
2 Sandy Road, Erith, Kent DA8 1FJ

pageCache.pageTitle: Religious Education  - Lime Wood Primary School
pageCache.text:
Religious Education
Our curriculum is delivered through the use of the Bexley Agreed Syllabus from EYFS to Y6. The syllabus is based around a key question approach, addressing three strands across each year group – believing, expressing and living, and sets out the suggested content for learning for each key question. If a particular religion is followed by a child in the class which is not included in the syllabus (for instance being a Sikh or a Jehovah’s Witness), then the syllabus can be adapted. In EYFS, RE is interweaved throughout their topics, and does not follow the Bexley Agreed Syllabus.
Throughout the teaching of Religious Education, children will have the opportunities to gain knowledge of how others live their lives, and it will equip them with the appropriate understanding to demonstrate respect for themselves and others as people with their own opinions, rights and social belonging. During our teaching of RE, we will incorporate some or all of the following: the use of religious artefacts, visits to places of worship, visitors to the school from different faiths, teaching approaches that promote Religious Education skills and a variety of ways for children to record their learning experiences.
Parents’ Right to Withdraw from Religious Education - In line with Department for Education guidance, parents have the right to withdraw their child from all or part of Religious Education (RE) lessons if they wish. If you are considering this, we encourage you to speak with the Headteacher first to discuss your views and ensure you have all the information you need. Should you choose to withdraw your child, the school will respect your decision and work with you to support appropriate alternative arrangements.

pageCache.text:
Music
We believe all children should receive engaging music lessons which include active participation and practical music-making at the heart of all learning. We ensure that through music our children will learn a host of transferable skills, particularly confidence and high self-esteem, which will support their self-expression and learning across all areas of the curriculum. This will also support their well-being and mental health.
Lessons include listening, composing, performing and appraising at the core.
Whole-class instrumental tuition enables the children to learn how to read musical notation.
Children appraise and analyse compositional features of music from different times and cultures and use this knowledge to inspire their own compositions.
